outcome: The general MLC conjecture (is the Mandelbrot set locally connected everywhere?) remains fully open, but Dudko and Lyubich's proof of MLC at Feigenbaum-type (period-doubling and complex-tripling) parameters — a preprint already posted before the window — was published in a refereed journal (Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS, vol. 143, pp. 97–141, online 2 June 2026) during the window, and a further special-case extension (Kahn–Kapiamba–Lyubich, 'MLC for parabolically bounded primitive renormalization', June 2026) newly settled MLC for another class of renormalizable parameters.
summary: Two distinct events fall inside the window, both extending — not resolving — the MLC conjecture. First, Dudko and Lyubich's 'MLC at Feigenbaum points' (arXiv:2309.02107, v1 Sep 2023, v2 Dec 2023 — both before the frozen revision) received a v3 revision on 29 Dec 2025 and was then formally published, with a DOI and page numbers, in Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS vol. 143 (2026), pp. 97–141, online 2 June 2026 (confirmed by directly fetching the journal's article page). This upgrades the paper's status from preprint to expert-vetted (peer-reviewed, published in a top journal), so I record it, but the underlying mathematical result — MLC at Feigenbaum-type period-doubling and complex-tripling parameters — was already circulating before 26 January 2024 and is not itself a new event in the window; only its formal publication is. Second, and squarely inside the window on its own preprint date, Kahn, Kapiamba and Lyubich posted 'MLC for parabolically bounded primitive renormalization' (arXiv:2606.27272, submitted 25 June 2026, directly fetched), proving a priori bounds and local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set for a further class of infinitely renormalizable parameters (primitive renormalization type, approaching the cusp of M) using new tools (Thin-Thick Decomposition, Value Calculus, Wanderers Theorem, Wave Lemma). This is a genuine new case of MLC settled within the window — a restriction of the stated question to a specific parameter class, which is squarely a 'case of the problem' under §3.1, not a variant. Neither paper claims, nor is treated by any source as claiming, the general MLC conjecture (local connectivity of the entire Mandelbrot set). Wikipedia's live article and a Dec 2025 ICM 2026 survey by Dudko (arXiv:2512.24171, ICM survey, ~confirmed via search, framed explicitly as consolidating 'recent developments' rather than a resolution) both state the general conjecture is still open. No credible AI/LLM/automated-theorem-proving involvement was found in any of this work: the Dudko-Lyubich and Kahn-Kapiamba-Lyubich papers were directly checked (acknowledgements/full text) and contain no AI attribution; a crowdsourced Lean-formalization tracker (Prove2Me) lists MLC as an open target with no claim of AI-driven progress on it. I classify the record as 'partial' with 'confirmed' direction because the settled pieces (Feigenbaum-type and now parabolically-bounded-primitive-renormalization parameters) are additional territory carved out of the open general conjecture in the direction the conjecture predicts (local connectivity holds at these parameters), not a refutation.
competing_reading: One could argue this record should be 'open_stale' rather than 'partial', on the grounds that the only work whose mathematical content predates the window is the Dudko-Lyubich Feigenbaum result (posted Sept/Dec 2023), and that its 2026 journal publication is a purely bureaucratic event that shouldn't count as the decisive event. Under that reading the decisive event would instead be the June 2026 Kahn-Kapiamba-Lyubich paper alone, which is what I used to date `event` — so the two readings converge on the same status ('partial') and event date; the disagreement would only be about whether to also cite the IHÉS publication as a second, independent event. I chose to include it because it is itself dated inside the window (per §6.3, journal publication is normally excluded as a lagging indicator, but here the preprint's own underlying claim already existed before the window, so the publication date is the first point at which this specific fact — MLC proven and vetted at Feigenbaum points — became an established, expert-checked event) rather than to avoid double-counting a single underlying mathematical result under two dates.
what_would_settle_it: Direct confirmation (already obtained) of the IHÉS publication date and DOI, and of the Kahn-Kapiamba-Lyubich arXiv submission date, both independently fetched and cross-checked above; no further evidence is needed to settle the classification.
